title: Ignore-and-Rot (Ignored Failing Tests)
pattern: Test cases marked with disable annotations (`#[ignore]` in Rust, `@Ignore` in Java, or commented out) without linked bug tracking IDs or explanations.
why_bad: Failing tests that are ignored are easily forgotten. Left in the codebase, they rot as APIs shift, reducing developer discipline and eventually leading to the abandonment of the test suite [69, 269].
detection: The presence of `#[ignore]` attributes in the test suite without comments referencing active bug tickets or dates.
counterexample: Temporarily ignoring a test with a clear comment linking to a tracking issue: `#[ignore] // TODO(issue-1204): Fix flaky socket buffer on CI`.
fix: Fix the test immediately, or if the underlying feature is permanently obsolete, delete the test and its code completely [69, 225].
source:
*   *The Pragmatic Programmer*, "Software Entropy / Spew of ignored tests" (p. 269) [269, 572]
*   *Clean Code*, "Ignore / Rotting tests" (p. 123) [63, 69]
